title: Same-radius adjacent-shift control is equivalent to a lower weight-ratio bound and excludes factorial weights

weight_tradeoff.general_energy: For positive weights w_n define G_w=sum_n w_nH_n and S_w=sum_n w_nsqrt(H_nH_(n+1)).
weight_tradeoff.criterion: A cutoff-independent inequality S_w<=CG_w for every nonnegative sequence H holds if and only if q=sup_n sqrt(w_n/w_(n+1)) is finite. Weighted Cauchy and 2uv<=u^2+v^2 give C<=q; two-tier tests give the converse lower bound C>=q/2.
weight_tradeoff.factorial_obstruction: For w_n=rho^(2n)/n!, sqrt(w_n/w_(n+1))=sqrt(n+1)/rho, so the adjacent shift is unbounded at every fixed rho. This is the abstract form of K1569's concentrated-tier witness.
weight_tradeoff.geometric_control: For geometric weights w_n=rho^(2n), the ratio is 1/rho and same-radius shift control holds. But geometric weights are a strictly stronger charge-tail norm than factorial weights and do not inherit K1450's exponential-generating-function closure for free.
weight_tradeoff.leibniz_tradeoff: Any exact exponential-generating Leibniz normalization w_n^(1/2) proportional to rho^n/n! has ratio sqrt(w_n/w_(n+1))=(n+1)/rho and therefore fails the criterion even more strongly. A weight change cannot simultaneously preserve that exact factorial product bookkeeping and make the adjacent shift bounded at one fixed radius.
weight_tradeoff.consequence: Within the admitted analytic hierarchy, the honest routes are radius expenditure, additional charge-tail regularity, or a structural gauge/spacetime cancellation. Renaming the factorial weight cannot remove the shift.
weight_tradeoff.scope_guard: This is a sequence-space classification. It does not exclude all modified energies, nonlinear cancellations, dispersive estimates, gauge choices or global PDE mechanisms.
